question: Does the small native-host-envelope overlap excess remaining after mean climate conditioning persist after seasonal climate proxies and subcontinental introduction geography are held fixed?
primary_panel: 191 butterflies with positive observed expansion and the minimum host-taxonomy consistency filter; not a complete-host-record panel
primary_endpoint: Observed minus null mean introduced host-by-butterfly-by-region incidences inside the fixed native-known-host resource envelope (B)
secondary_endpoints: unique newly resource-covered butterfly x region units U
introduced-host overlap D outside native envelopes
common_conditions: plant and regional introduction margins within every allowed block

additional_conditions.seasonal: within-continent medians of BIO7 annual temperature range and BIO15 precipitation seasonality; not plant phenology
additional_conditions.geographic: official WGSRPD level2 subcontinental region; not exact physical-distance matching

input_guard: Any stored climate variable exactly equal to 65535 is flagged as a possible encoding ceiling, not asserted to be missing. Such regions and missing-climate regions are retained but frozen individually in EVERY comparison model and omitted from cutpoint calibration. No imputation or removal of host records.
interpretation_boundary: Nested nulls change the randomization space. Attenuation is not causal climate mediation. Null-like results do not prove no biological mechanism. Tight blocks may limit identifiability; report focal-edge movement beside residuals. No local larval use, fitness, phenological synchrony or demographic stability claim. The GEB PR #38 remains untouched.
